clue.text: Particular abhorrence of reading tape translation first

indicators.note: first says the rearranged tape comes at the front, ahead of the other piece
translation turns the word tape into different letters, as one language is rendered into another

parts.note: a reading is an interpretation, or version, of a text

explanation.surface: Someone's pet hatred is having to read a translation of a tape.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet hate is something a person dislikes especially, their own particular object of loathing.

clue.text: For containing water, dam river

parts.note: a dam is a mother animal, here a female sheep

explanation.surface: A dam built across a river to hold back water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dam' suggests a barrier on a river, but it is a mother animal, here a ewe.
explanation.definitionFit: A jug is a vessel for holding water, typically paired with a washbasin.

clue.text: A set of books, one, isn't commending

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A collection of books, one of which offers no praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Being against something means opposing it rather than praising it.

clue.text: Middle course sought by outsiders?

explanation.surface: A compromise path that people on the fringe go looking for.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the main dish of a meal; the second is the right of admission that those outside want.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a dish served between other courses, and also the right of admission to a society or place.

clue.text: After Times upheaval, managed health resort payment received not quite clear gain

indicators.note: an upheaval throws things into disorder, so the letters of Times are scrambled

parts.note: to have run something is to have managed it
a spa is a resort visited for its healing waters
rent is money paid to and received by a landlord

explanation.surface: Following turmoil at the Times newspaper, a spa's earnings brought only murky gains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upheaval' turns TIMES into SEMIT; 'gain' is left over in the clue as printed and does no work.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that lets light through only partly is somewhat translucent, so not fully see-through.

clue.text: Having to be paid around mid-morning.

indicators.note: around says the phrase for being due goes outside the other piece

parts.note: money owing is still to be paid

indicators.note: mid- attached to morning asks for the central letter of that word

explanation.surface: A bill falling due at about the middle of the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: To possess something is to have it as one's property.

clue.text: Hide in tub in order to get free

indicators.note: putting the words in order arranges their letters afresh

explanation.surface: Someone hides in a bath to escape.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without restraint is free in their behaviour, not held back by inhibitions.

clue.text: Outstanding vocalist making- seasonal appearance

parts.note: outstanding is read as standing outside: a singer who stands at doors in the street at Christmas

explanation.surface: A star singer turns up for a festive concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' reads as 'excellent', but here it means standing out of doors, as Christmas singers do going door to door.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas brings groups who sing festive songs from door to door, standing outside.

clue.text: Indian canine, disoriented, loses direction

indicators.note: disoriented means jumbled about, so the letters of canine are mixed up

parts.note: NE, north-east, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A lost dog in India wanders off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' takes NE out of CANINE; the remaining letters CAIN are mixed up by 'disoriented'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Incas were indigenous people of Peru, American Indians in the older usage.

clue.text: Flowers enclosed-no stems broken

parts.note: pent, as in pent up, means shut in

indicators.note: broken means the letters of no stems are smashed and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Flowers in a vase arrive with all their stalks snapped.
explanation.definitionFit: These are garden plants of the figwort family with tubular blooms, often called beardtongues.

clue.text: An oriental chest that's made of iron

indicators.note: made of says the letters of iron are worked into something new

explanation.surface: A Japanese chest constructed from metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A small Japanese box with compartments, hung from the sash, is a kind of oriental case.

clue.text: Penthouse source of super poetry

indicators.note: the words are raw material from which the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A top-floor flat inspires excellent verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A penthouse is a flat on the top floor of a building.

clue.text: Upsetting histrionics, with this disease

indicators.note: upsetting knocks the letters of histrionics over into a new order

explanation.surface: Theatrical fuss over an illness proves distressing.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an illness caused by roundworms caught from eating undercooked pork.

clue.text: King of deep resolution

annotationWithheld.why: King of deep resolution (7): no wordplay can be built from the clue as held; resolution looks like an anagram indicator with its fodder missing

clue.text: Heavenly body turning women on

indicators.note: turning means the letters of women on are rearranged

explanation.surface: A celestial beauty who excites women.
explanation.definitionFit: The moon at the start of its cycle is a heavenly body barely visible in the sky.

clue.text: Cleaned festering wound

indicators.note: festering means going bad, so the letters of cleaned are disordered

explanation.surface: A cut that was washed has started to go septic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' looks like an injury, but it is the past tense of wind, meaning twisted together.
explanation.definitionFit: Laced together means twined or wound round each other.

clue.text: Standard look for. an Indian

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
to see is to look

explanation.surface: A typical glance in search of someone from India.
explanation.definitionFit: A Parsi is a member of the Zoroastrian community in India descended from Persian settlers.

clue.text: This coarse-grained rock singes in eruption

indicators.note: in eruption means blown apart, so the letters of singes are scattered

explanation.surface: Volcanic heat scorches a rough stone.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a banded metamorphic rock with a coarse texture.

clue.text: Late with message of ecclesiastic ban

parts.note: ex means former, and late can mean former, as in a late president
a communication is a message

explanation.surface: A belated message about a church prohibition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cut off from the sacraments of the church is a ban imposed by clerics.

clue.text: Behold sari twined round member of the crew

indicators.note: round says the twisted letters go about the other piece
twined means twisted, so the letters of sari are wound into a new order

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Look at the sari wrapped around a ship's hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twined' scrambles the sari's letters to SAIR, and 'round' wraps that about the old exclamation for look; 'member' suggests a limb or club member, but it is a person in the crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaman is one of the people working on a ship.

clue.text: About to get small. tip for delivery

parts.note: re means about or concerning
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a cue is a hint or tip-off

explanation.surface: A small gratuity is about to be paid for a delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' suggests a gratuity, but it is a hint or prompt.
explanation.definitionFit: Delivery can mean being saved or set free from danger.

clue.text: About to. give up: and go back

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to cede is to give up or surrender

explanation.surface: Ready to surrender and retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw is to go back or move away.

clue.text: Argue with justification

explanation.surface: Make a case backed by good grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue logically is to think it through, and a justification is a ground or cause for something.

clue.text: Want label, put in the other way round, then wiped out

indicators.note: put in says the turned label goes inside the word for want

parts.note: to want is to need

indicators.note: the other way round means the word for label is read backwards

parts.note: a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A label stuck on back to front and then erased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the other way round' reverses the label to GAT, and 'put in' places it inside the word for want; 'Want' reads as lack, not desire.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nullified has been cancelled or wiped out.

clue.text: Ring in an order for an instrument.

indicators.note: in says the circle is placed inside the honour

parts.note: the OBE is the Order of the British Empire, a British honour
O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: Ringing up to order a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a woodwind instrument with a double reed.

clue.text: Small piece of wood pine

explanation.surface: A little bit of wood from a pine tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine' looks like the tree, but it is the verb meaning to grieve.
explanation.definitionFit: A fret is a ridge on a guitar neck, often wooden, and to pine is to worry or grieve.

clue.text: Manx bird-one much revered'

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the word for bird loses its last letter

parts.note: a heron is a wading bird

explanation.surface: A bird from the Isle of Man that is highly esteemed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Manx cat, from the Isle of Man off Britain, is tailless, so 'Manx' means docked.
explanation.definitionFit: A person admired for courage or achievement is idolised by many.

clue.text: On the way. in, duck then rise awkwardly,'seeing those who. encouraged the 'crime

parts.note: access is a way in
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

indicators.note: awkwardly means the letters of rise are arranged clumsily

explanation.surface: On the way in, someone ducks and stands up clumsily, spotting the people behind a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' is a cricket score of zero, hence O; 'awkwardly' turns RISE into RIES.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, accomplices are people who help or abet a crime without committing it themselves.

clue.text: Boy brought to book. by degrees

explanation.surface: A lad gradually being held to account.
explanation.walkthrough: Eric, or Little by Little (1858) is a Victorian school novel by F. W. Farrar: the boy appears in a book titled by degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a boy's name, and the title of a Victorian novel subtitled Little by Little.

clue.text: A race to get there after tide's turned?

indicators.note: after places the people piece behind the rearranged letters
turned means the letters of the tide's word are rearranged

parts.note: a nation is a people or race

explanation.surface: A people hurrying to arrive once the tide has changed.
explanation.definitionFit: The place one is heading for is the end point of a journey.
